reviewNote: Review 2026-11-04 from a paired visual sweep of all 12 paper and 36 scheme pages (paper pages 11-12 are blank; scheme pages 1-4 are the SEC cover, the note on published schemes, the title page and the notes and index, and pages 34-36 blank or the back cover; scheme page numbers here are the PDF’s, two ahead of the printed ones; this scheme prints no Summary of Mark Allocations, so every tariff is read beside its part). The old-syllabus paper: Section A nine short questions (answer six), Section B eight long questions (answer four) numbered 1-8 again, keyed B1-B8 as the Atlas numbers them. 71 routes for 80 printed asks (18 Section A + 62 Section B), 36 raw directive lines classified. Every stem and ask is sliced from the paper and every marking point from the scheme (econ_2015_ol.py). Four cards cover more than one printed ask because the scheme prices them together: Section A Q5(a)-(b), Section B Q1(b)(ii)-(iii), Q2(a)(i)-(iii) and Q5(c)(i)-(iii). Section B Q4(c)(ii) is one route per economist. Section B Q3(b)(i) prices the national minimum wage 6: the scheme prints 7 beside it but sets it as 4 + 2, and only 6 fits the paper’s (24).
